Docs/Data & replay

Data & replay

The release contains 100 replay-successful demonstrations for each of 30 canonical stage tasks.

3,000episodes
9.1 hteleoperation
20 Hzrecording
100per stage

Two-stage review

Episodes first enter a pending store with a reviewable MP4. Interactive or success-based review then exports accepted episodes to per-hand LeRobot directories.

Frame schema

FeatureMeaning
observation.stateRobot proprioception and task state.
actionAbsolute arm and hand joint targets.
observation.environment_stateFlat environment state for restoration and re-rendering.
next.successPer-step result from the environment success predicate.
episode.seedSeed used for exact reset and replay.

Validation

Accepted data is restored in a fresh simulator, rendered offline, and replayed open-loop from the recorded initial state. Only replay-successful trajectories enter the release set.

Data collection pipeline

VR and glove inputs are converted into joint targets. Recording, review, export and replay validation connect human demonstration collection to offline multi-view rendering.

Read the paper's data collection overview →

Hand usage across six motion families

Opening and closing, grasping and placement, insertion and assembly, twisting and screwing, pressing, and scooping and pouring produce distinct patterns of hand contact and joint motion.

From accepted episodes to replayable data

The paper reports 4,112 accepted episodes and 3,222 open-loop replay successes (about 78%). The released set selects 100 replay-successful demonstrations per stage, for 3,000 episodes and 9.1 hours.

Paper replay success by motion category; stage tasks are weighted equally within each category.
Motion familyReplay success
Opening and closing98%
Grasping and placement84%
Insertion and assembly65%
Twisting and screwing87%
Pressing83%
Scooping and pouring74%

Trajectory diversity

Across stages, mean palm path length spans 0.35–2.04 m; mean pairwise palm-trajectory distance spans 3.3–10.2 cm. More sustained contact is associated with lower replay success (Spearman ρ = −0.58 for contact ratio, p < 0.001).
